# Arithmetic and combinatorial research: P026–P030 source review

These are **five mathematical research entries**, not five claims to previously unknown open problems. Each dossier contains a precise object and a falsification gate. A bounded source search identifies nearby mathematics; specialist priority checking remains necessary.

## P026 — Square generation in bipartite prime-sum graphs

**Question.** Is the F_2 cycle space of the two-copy bipartite graph with i+j prime generated by its four-cycles, for every n? If so, how many squares suffice to fill arbitrary cycles?

**Exact evidence:** For every integer 2≤n≤60, all edges and four-cycles were enumerated and the GF(2) boundary rank was computed. At n=60 there are 843 edges, cycle-space dimension 724 and 17,144 squares; their span has rank exactly 724. **Nothing beyond n=60 has been proved.**

**Relevant known work:** [Prime Sum Graphs and the Induced Trees They Contain](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00373-025-02999-2) concerns the number-theoretic host graph; [Ohsugi–Hibi, Toric Ideals Generated by Quadratic Binomials](https://doi.org/10.1006/jabr.1999.7918) places square-cycle generation in the classical graph-toric-ideal framework. **Priority risk:** a general chordal-bipartite or toric-ideal result may settle the square-generation problem. Need check whether our host satisfies a sufficient hypothesis, and not confuse mod-2 generation with integral generation or fundamental-group triviality.

## P027 — Maximum primitive-set exchanges

**Question.** Mixing and possible cutoff for single-dyadic-chain heat-bath sampling from *all* maximum-size primitive subsets of [2n].

**New internal calculation:** An explicit exponent representation leads to exact exchange distances equal to coordinatewise Hamming distance and diameter

$$
\mathrm{diam}(G_n)=\#\{u\text{ odd}:u\le n/2\}
+\#\{u\text{ odd}:2n/3<u\le n\}
=\frac{5n}{12}+O(1).
$$

See [full internally proved theorem](../theorems/P027-primitive-set-exchange-diameter.md) and [complete small finite graph checks](../experiments/P027_primitive_exchange_diameter.py).

**Closest original subject:** [Liu–Pach–Palincza, *The number of maximum primitive sets of integers*](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548321000018), which proves the asymptotic exponential number of states. The dyadic decomposition is well known and is **not** new. Also compare [heat-bath random walks with Markov bases](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aam.2017.08.002), and [rowmotion Markov chains](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0196885823001847). **Novelty:** the elementary distance theorem and any mixing claim need specialist verification; no sharp mixing-time theorem is presently claimed.

## P028 — Thinned divisor order complexes and a zeta deformation

**Question.** Mean asymptotics and random fluctuations of reduced Euler characteristics after independently retaining each integer in [2,N] with probability p.

**Exact observation:** For f_r(n) the number of ordered factorizations into r factors at least 2,

$$
\phi_p(n)=\sum_{r\ge1}(-1)^{r-1}p^r f_r(n),\quad
\mathbb E\widetilde\chi=-1+\sum_{n=2}^N\phi_p(n),
$$

and, initially for large real part of s,

$$
\sum_{n\ge2}\phi_p(n)n^{-s}
=\frac{p(\zeta(s)-1)}{1+p(\zeta(s)-1)}.
$$

At p=1 this recovers the classical Mertens sum with a minus sign. The identity is a **direct ordered-factorization / Dirichlet-inverse computation**, not novel. Exact independent subset calculations at rational p and N≤9 match it.

**References:** [DLMF Dirichlet convolution](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.5), [Bolognini–Macchia–Ventura–Welker](https://doi.org/10.1137/15M1049142), [Brown on probabilistic zeta and posets](https://doi.org/10.1006/jabr.1999.8221), and [ordered divisor factorizations](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11139-018-0093-9). **Novelty risk high:** ask whether the complete asymptotic analysis is already known under weighted Möbius or Dirichlet inverse functions, rather than assuming a new invariant.

## P029 — Prime-supported permutation X-ray fibers

**Question.** Is there an absolute move-size bound that connects all permutations with prime i+σ(i) and a fixed histogram of those prime sums?

The underlying *X-ray* (anti-diagonal histogram) is **classical**, treated by [Bebeacua–Mansour–Postnikov–Severini (2005)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.endm.2005.05.063) and in [Del Lungo's tomography paper (2002)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-3975(02)00015-4). The prime support constraint and fiber moves are an additional restriction, but may be subsumed by a known Markov basis.

**Exact obstruction:** No nontrivial two-position swap preserves the exact histogram. At n=4, the two distinct prime-supported permutations (2,3,4,1) and (4,1,2,3) have histogram {3,5,5,7} and require changing four positions. Small fiber counts were obtained by complete search through n=13. **Status:** high collision risk, reserve rather than flagship.

## P030 — Simultaneously prime sums and differences

**Question.** Does every even N≥8 have a partition into pairs {a,b} such that both a+b and |a−b| are prime?

**Exact obstruction:** Every edge has opposite-parity endpoints, so odd N is impossible. Exact matchings exist for **every even N=8,10,…,400**; no such perfect matching exists for N=2,4,6. These are finite certificates, not a proof of the conjecture.

**Direct prior art:** [OEIS A227050](https://oeis.org/A227050) counts circular Hamiltonian arrangements with *the same two primality constraints*. Its positive instances already imply some finite pairing instances; **do not represent them as original constructions**. Also see [OEIS A073364](https://oeis.org/A073364) for the easier sum-only permutation host and [prime-sum graph structural results](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00373-025-02999-2). The existence of Hamiltonian arrangements for all sufficiently large even N would imply the pairing statement immediately, so that literature must be audited first.

## Editorial assessment

P027 and P028 have the clearest immediate **mathematical structure**, although their baseline formulas may be derivable from classical machinery. P026 and P030 ask crisp arithmetic graph questions with extensive exact finite checks and could produce interesting number-theoretic proofs. P029 offers a legitimate constrained-tomography direction but has **particularly high historical collision risk**.

None of these problems has been externally certified original or unproved. The independently proved P027 diameter formula is included as a *theorem note*, not as a still-open conjecture. The intended open part is the random-walk mixing behaviour.

For the catalogue's current interpretation and contribution process, see the [main README](../README.md#status-and-scope) and [contributor guide](../CONTRIBUTING.md).
